readnow.text: No new chapter today. Keep Chapters 13 to 15 open in your book as you study Fleischman's voice.

warmup.text: Today a very different poem: Carl Sandburg's Fog, only six lines long. Read it slowly. Then compare it with Windy Nights. Same five parts, used to do the opposite thing.

words.text: Explain the three endings in your own words, and add each ending to a base. Pick an option on the vocabulary choice board. The last eight notches bring the bucket out of the hole.

reading.text: Read the five voice techniques. Find one example of each kind in Chapters 13 to 15. Then answer the voice questions, and pick the technique your own adventure needs most.

assignment.text: Read your paragraph out loud one last time. Put the final version in the box, with one sentence about your biggest change. Then copy your work into Canvas.

game.title: Climb Out of the Coyote Hole
game.sub: This week's word game · 8 notches today
game.look: A coyote hole is a deep shaft miners dug straight down to bedrock, where heavy gold settles. Each right answer hauls the bucket of pay dirt up one notch of the rope. A wrong answer lets loose dirt slide it back down one notch.

do: Read the clue.
Tap the word that fits.
Tap Haul it up for the next clue.
how.why: A suffix is spelled the same way every time, and a word family keeps its base. Knowing both keeps your spelling right.

game.doneLine: Four days, thirty-two notches. The pay dirt is out of the hole.

rounds.why: joy + ous: the y stays, because a vowel comes before it.
imagine drops its e, then + ative.
rounds.miss: Drop the e, then add -ative with an a.
Spell similar first: s, i, m, i, l, a, r.
One letter of adventure drops before the ending.

rounds.clue: Which word is in the prospect family?
rounds.why: prospect + us: a paper that describes a plan.
rounds.miss: prosperity looks close, but it comes from prosper.

rounds.clue: Which word is in the same family as luck?
rounds.miss: Look for the whole word luck inside.

rounds.why: persuade: the d becomes s before -ive.
rounds.miss: The d in persuade changes before the ending.

virtue.name: integrity
virtue.title: The moment of most integrity this week
virtue.intro: Look back at Chapters 13 to 15. Tap the moment you think shows integrity the most.

options.t: Jack pays for the neckties with half his nugget rather than go back on his word (Chapter 13).
Praiseworthy promises he will be back to fight the Mountain Ox: “I gave my word, didn't I?” (Chapter 14).
The road agent gives back the coat he stole (Chapter 15).
